questions.q: What index type does PostgreSQL create by default when no type is specified in CREATE INDEX?
options: GiST
Hash
B-tree
GIN
questions.explain: B-tree is PostgreSQL's default index type, used for equality and range comparisons and sorting, just like a SQL Server nonclustered index.

questions.q: What is a GIN index specifically built to index?
options: Foreign key relationships
The individual elements inside a composite value, such as words in text or keys in JSONB
Physical row order on disk
Only integer primary keys
questions.explain: GIN (Generalized Inverted Index) indexes what's inside a value — like a book index indexing words, not page numbers — used for full-text search and JSONB containment.

questions.q: What kind of query does a GiST index on a range type make efficient, per this lesson?
options: Full-text search queries
Exact equality lookups only
Overlap queries, such as finding bookings whose time range overlaps a given range
Sorting by a numeric column
questions.explain: GiST supports overlap, containment, and nearest-comparison queries on ranges and geometric types, which a strict-ordering B-tree can't answer efficiently.

questions.q: What key structural difference does this lesson note between PostgreSQL and SQL Server indexing?
options: SQL Server has no concept of a B-tree index
PostgreSQL has no automatically-maintained clustered index that physically orders table rows the way SQL Server does
PostgreSQL tables cannot have more than one index
PostgreSQL indexes cannot be created on more than one column
questions.explain: Every PostgreSQL index, including B-tree, is a separate structure pointing back at heap rows; CLUSTER can reorder rows once but isn't automatically maintained like a SQL Server clustered index.

questions.q: Why would a plain B-tree index not help a query checking whether a JSONB column contains a specific key/value pair?
options: B-tree indexes only work on text columns
B-tree indexes cannot be created on JSONB columns at all
A B-tree indexes the value as a whole for ordering, not the individual elements contained inside it
JSONB columns are always unindexed in PostgreSQL
questions.explain: Containment questions are about what's inside the value, which is exactly what a GIN index is built to answer efficiently instead.
